prototypeScope: V1.22 delta package, the ankle rework: Orange plate with the two ankle bases and two ankle sides, Black plate with the two 10.4 mm ankle sleeves, Yellow plate with three pairs of slip-fit feet (one to fit, two spare for sole experiments). V1.20 is printed and the V1.21 molds were printed in black on 2026-10-19 (Shawn).
knownFitBoundary: Ankle: the side screws are self-tapping in 1.6 mm printed pilots, hand snug only; the sleeve has about 0.4 mm of diametral running clearance in CAD, so a little side play is by design; printed hole sizes are not measured yet. Feet: 0.2 mm CAD clearance per side to the base and side; if a printed pair is tight, sand the socket walls of the foot, never force it. Not fitted on the robot yet.
processOverrideReason: Stock profiles on every plate (brims per object by the pipeline R1 rule or the manifest objectSettings).

parts.sourceFrame: ankle-redesign-20261007 local frame of the left ankle base (mm; motor shaft = local z through the origin)
parts.poseOrigin: local +X down (10/07 candidate: big gusset end on the bed): Local +X down: the big gusset end face (81.1 mm2, tip 2.8 deg, 36.5 mm tall) on the bed, exactly the 10/07 candidate pose (the 10/07 package was never printed: its README says no print has been started). It is the only family of poses where the motor mating face, the four output screw seats, the slot walls, the post register faces and the pilot bores all stand vertical or face up, so none of them touches support on either machine (0 mm2 resting on support, 0 mm of support inside pilots, slots and output holes). The mirror pose (-X down) is equivalent on the functional faces but puts more of the foot slip-fit block on support (22.7 / 53.3 mm2 against 8.2 / 26.6) and has the same Bambu brim notch. The screen favourite (-Z tilted onto the foot facets, 316 mm2 contact, no brim) is rejected because it turns the output seats down onto support (35.5 mm2 on Elegoo) and fills the slot channels and pilots with support on Bambu.

parts.changeReason: Replaces the printed community-66.stl (stock object 20, the left one-piece ankle bracket) together with ankle_cheek_left. Shawn 2026-10-19: the one-piece bracket is a closed fork; the lower link with its servo and sleeve cannot come in from above (assembly-path-investigation.md), so it was spread and pressed on, loading the ankle servo at every fitting. The base keeps the motor-output holes and the foot block of the stock bracket; with the side off, the link-servo-sleeve package lifts straight out (ankle-split-check.json packageLiftSideOff 0 mm3 left, the 0.137 mm3 source mating-face slab right). The V1.22 slip-fit foot seats on it as on the stock bracket (footSeat).

parts.sourceFrame: ankle-redesign-20261007 local frame of the left ankle side (mm; motor shaft = local z through the origin)
parts.poseOrigin: local +Z down (10/07 candidate: tab tops on the bed, lip up): Local +Z down: the two 7 x 4 mm tab tops (57.6 mm2, two islands) on the bed, lip up, the 10/07 candidate pose (never printed). The bearing pocket wall stands vertical and carries 0 mm of support inside it on both machines, the capture lip faces up at print z 5.6 mm and is a clean top surface, the tongues print as upright ribs (49-54 mm of toolpath, the 0.4 mm rib is printed), the tab register faces are vertical walls, and the d2.3 clearance bores are bridged with 0 mm of support inside. The price is that the part is not self-standing (tip -44.3 deg): the body floats 4.1 mm above the bed on support and the whole exterior top (272-280 mm2) rests on support. The only other viable pose (-Z down) turns the capture lip down onto support (22.6 mm2 on Bambu, 966-1052 mm of support inside the pocket) and fails the brim review on both machines, so the cosmetic exterior takes the scars instead of the lip.

parts.changeReason: New part, with ankle_base_left replacing the printed community-66.stl (stock object 20). The removable side of the split ankle: it closes along the shaft onto the sleeve until its two tabs meet the solid base posts, and two M2 x 8 TAP from above (1.6 mm pilots in the base, 2.3 mm clearance in the side) hold and locate it. With the foot off it slides outward clear of the base and the package (ankle-split-check.json sidePath); with the foot on it is captured. DESIGN-NOTES.md in ankle-redesign-20261007/.

parts.changeReason: Replaces the printed community-44.stl (stock object 32, the left foot). Shawn 2026-10-19: the orange ankle bracket and the yellow foot press together so tightly that they cannot be taken apart, and each fitting loads the ankle servo. The socket that holds the bracket's lower block is opened 0.2 mm sideways along the straight insertion path, the two snap tongues are deleted (the cut had left them 0.6-0.7 mm thin flakes with no hook) and the heel well they stood in is filled to the wall tops; the faces the bracket rests on stay, so it seats where it seats now, with 0.14-0.20 mm play each way and free lift-off. The toe M2 x 6 TAP holds the foot. The same socket fits the V1.22 ankle base and side (ankle-split-check.json footSeat). Sole unchanged below 4 mm (the hot-glue molds fit). foot-slipfit-20261019/slipfit-check.json.
